posts:
Nous Research hits $1.5B valuation with $90M Series B.
Evidence: $90M raised, 24M clones, enterprise pivot, $100M ARR target.
#TechCrunch #ArtificialIntelligence

Nous Research raised a $90M Series B at a $1.5B valuation to bring its popular open-source Hermes Agent to enterprise business users.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

While open-source roots built massive adoption, the $90M raise ties the project directly to venture capital return mandates and enterprise data locking.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.5, +0.4) — Conditional Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Redemption.
Open-source AI innovation scales successfully, though commercialization pressures shift focus toward enterprise monetization.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.35, z: 1)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Open Source Growth: PASS (+0.9, +0.8) — Massive developer adoption.
- Enterprise Monetization: COND (+0.3, +0.2) — Shifts toward corporate lock-in.
Nous Research secured a $90M Series B led by Robot Ventures with backing from Nvidia and Samsung, pushing valuation to $1.5B while launching enterprise tools.

The Bright Side:
High-performance AI tools become accessible and customizable for developers globally, driving massive efficiency gains.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing open-source developer enthusiasm (WHO) with corporate enterprise licensing extraction (WHY).

Social Physics Analysis:
Nous runs a hybrid loop: community-driven open source adoption transitioning into a high-stakes enterprise monetization maneuver.

The Trajectory: The Path of Redemption.
When you map open-source community ideals against massive venture funding rounds, it plots a trajectory toward commercialized utility.

The Unavoidable Truth: Open-source models can achieve massive commercial valuations and enterprise traction.

The Unavoidable Lie: Venture-backed AI infrastructure remains entirely independent of corporate monetization demands.

Alethekanon:
Open-source momentum builds immense valuation, yet institutional capital inevitably demands commercial extraction 🌐

Awwthekanon:
It is inspiring to see developer-driven projects thrive, bringing powerful tools into the hands of creators everywhere.

Brothekanon:
From open-source pet project to a billion-dollar enterprise player overnight. Wild times in AI.

Spirithekanon:
"Better is a handful with quietness than both hands full together, grasping for wind." Ecclesiastes 4:6 PASS (Spiritual Vector)
Balancing open community collaboration prevents the hollow pursuit of endless corporate accumulation.

Posted:

Nous Research, the startup developing the open source Hermes Agent, has raised a $90 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, confirming TechCrunch’s earlier reporting.

The round was led by Robot Ventures, with participation from other backers including Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung, and 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner. The new financing brings the three-year-old startup’s total funding to $158 million.

Popular among developers and individuals, the open source Hermes Agent has been cloned more than 24 million times, driving roughly 2.5% of global AI token usage, according to the startup’s estimates.

The capital will fund Nous Research’s push into the enterprise sector with “Hermes for Businesses,” allowing companies to deploy customized AI agents that can handle multi-step workflows while keeping their data private and secure.

Nous was at roughly $36 million in annualized revenue by mid-September 2026 and expects to pass $100 million before the end of 2026, The Wall Street Journal reported.
